items.title: 61531_Juan Tizol oral history interview
items.q: in reading Stanley Dance's interview with you

ctx.x: Right now, I can't think of anything else; no, I can't remember nothing. I know we were terrific everywhere we went; everywhere in Europe.

Yesterday when we were talking, you were telling me about when Harry James called you to join his band, we didn't mention Woodie Herman, and in reading Stanley Dance's interview with you, I see that you had already made arrangements to go with Woodie Herman? Tell me about that.

Yes. I told Duke that I was going, when I was getting ready to quit, that I had signed with Woodie Herman to go with him, and later on when what's his name -- when Harry James called me, I had quit the band and Harry James had called me to go with him, I told Woodie Herman to see if he didn't mind to let me off, because after all, I wanted to go home, which I hadn't been in a whole year, almost. I could be there, and I wanted to see my wife, and I'd be back in Washington.
